title: BOS-723 — a daemon that accepts the socket and never answers now hits a bound: the board says so and recovers itself, and opening a chat lands on a dismissible error instead of an endless launching line

scenes.title: A wedged daemon takes the board to the named, self-recovering daemon-down screen instead of leaving a stale table on screen forever

waitFor.label: the seeded board is up before anything is wedged, so what follows replaces a working screen

steps.caption: The home session list is populated against a healthy daemon.

The daemon stops answering: it keeps accepting the socket connection but writes no response to any unary RPC. The window is deliberately longer than the wait that follows it, so a slow CI box cannot let the stall lapse mid-wait and turn a real failure into an unexplained timeout.

waitFor.label: the poll bound fires and the board says the daemon is unreachable — before BOS-723 the polls never returned and this screen was never reached

steps.caption: Three bounded poll failures later the board replaces the stale table with the daemon-down screen.

expect.label: the failure is named on screen rather than shown as a frozen table the user cannot tell apart from a quiet one
the remediation is a copy-able command, so a user whose daemon really is dead has a way out
the diagnose-first command is offered alongside the restart, so the user can look before they act

the action bar is on the SAME frame as the failure: one regex over one screen, so the healthy board's own [q]uit cannot stand in for it — after the bound fired the TUI is still drawing its keys, not hung

steps.caption: Named failure, both remediation commands, and a live action bar on one frame.

scenes.title: Opening a chat while the daemon withholds the record-chat answer lands on a bounded, dismissible error frame instead of the endless launching line

steps.caption: The daemon starts answering again so the user can navigate.

waitFor.label: the board is back, which is what makes the next navigation a normal one rather than a retry of the failure

steps.caption: The session list repopulates and the cursor is on the first seeded session.

waitFor.label: the chat picker is populated, so the chat about to be opened is a real one

steps.caption: The chat picker lists the session's conversations.
The daemon wedges on exactly the call attaching a chat depends on: RecordChat is accepted and never answered.

waitFor.label: the withheld RecordChat answer becomes a named, bounded error — without the bound the view stays on 'Launching …' for as long as the daemon stays wedged

steps.caption: The bound fires and the launching line is replaced by the failure it belongs to.

expect.label: the error names the operation that failed, not just a transport code

the way out is on the SAME frame as the record-chat failure: one regex over one screen, so the chat picker's own [esc] back cannot stand in for it — the bounded error frame itself is dismissible, not a dead end

steps.caption: A named failure with an escape hatch, reached without the user pressing anything to interrupt it.

The daemon goes fully unresponsive again while the user backs out. As in scene 1 the window outlasts the wait it gates, so scene 3's down-again check cannot be defeated by the stall quietly expiring first.
Leave the chat picker for the session board.

scenes.title: When the daemon starts answering again the board repopulates on its own — no restart, no keypress

waitFor.label: the board is genuinely down again, so the repopulation that follows is a recovery and not a screen that never left

steps.caption: Back on the board with the daemon still wedged: the daemon-down screen is showing. The wait is shorter than scene 2's 55s window even after two esc settles, so this can only fail because the screen never arrived — never because the wedge quietly lapsed underneath it.
The daemon starts answering again. Nothing else happens: boss is not restarted and no key is pressed for the rest of the scene.

waitFor.label: the first seeded session is back on the board with no user action — the failure screen was a state boss polls out of, not a dead end

steps.caption: The next successful poll clears the failure streak and the table is drawn again.

expect.label: a real session row from the daemon renders, so the recovered client is genuinely serving data
a second seeded row confirms the whole board came back, not a single lucky cell
the table chrome is back too, so this is the session board and not a fragment of the error screen

steps.caption: The board is fully populated again: an unreachable daemon is now a passing state, not a terminal one.
